# `device.place`

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask docs-gen` from crates/ew-commands/schemas/device.place.schema.json. Do not edit: change the source and regenerate. -->

`device.place` (`PlaceSymbol`, doc 06 §3.3): places a symbol and creates the device and function as the
target requires.

- `copies` (FT-656): library documents (`lib/` JSON form) embedded first, in the same transaction, as
  `part.assign` embeds its closure: each is checked as `library.embed` checks it, at `/copies/i`; a copy the
  project holds with the same hash is skipped, one it holds with another hash is refused ("update from library
  first", naming the item and the held version), the others are inserted. So a placement from a library is one
  undo step and the command replays without a library.
- The page and the symbol copy must exist. The representation is `{functions: [f], page, symbol,
  variant, pos, orient, rep_type}`; `rep_type` defaults to the symbol's.
- `new_device`: a device `{tag: {letter, counter: none}, kind}` and a main function `{def}`; `def` is
  `fndef` or the FnDef copy `v5(NS_LIBCOPY, library ‖ item)` of the symbol's `fndef` reference, which
  must be embedded (else rejected with a hint to pass `fndef`).
- `existing_function`: the function must exist and must not be an interruption point (`ip.place`).
- `join_device`: a new function of the device with the given role (a second main function is rejected
  by EW-INV-002).
- `from_part` (FR-UI-017, FR-DEV-017): a device `{tag: {letter, counter: none}, parts: [the part, quantity
  1]}` and one function per entry of the part copy's `function_template`, in template order (def: the entry's
  FnDef copy, which must be embedded; role main for `main`, else auxiliary; kind `black_box` when the FnDef's
  contact kind is `black_box`, else normal; `template_entry` the entry's index, so the CPs follow from that
  entry, doc 03 §7, FT-655); the representation
  draws entry `template`, the others stay unplaced. The symbol's FnDef must be entry `template`'s, and that
  entry must not be a black box (`box.black` places those).
- `new_terminal` (AC-28): one terminal of the strip, created as `terminal.add` creates it (the strip's letter,
  structure and the sequence number as counter; the next sequence number when `seq` is absent) with its main
  function `{def: the symbol's FnDef}`, then placed. With `part` (part-first placement of a terminal part) the
  terminal also gets `parts: [the part, quantity 1]`; the part copy must exist and, when it has a function
  template, its main entry's FnDef must be the symbol's.
- Every hint creates a wire `{a: the hint's CP, b: to, page}` without a route; the hint's symbol CP is
  mapped to a function CP as the derived pin map does (`(functions[0], fn_cp)`); an unknown symbol CP
  is rejected. A hint ending at a junction appends the wire to the junction's sequence; a hint ending
  on a point of a connection (`HintTarget::Split`) puts a new junction there, splits the connection at
  it (as `connection.draw` does) and ends the wire at the junction (the point must be on the page's
  connection grid). A hint whose function, junction or connection no longer exists is dropped and
  reported as a notice instead of failing the command.
- The effective `rep_type` must be one the page's type allows (doc 06 §2.2, `allowed_rep_types`);
  else the placement is rejected with the list of allowed types.

Rejected besides: a missing part copy or template index; a template without exactly one main entry (a device
has one main function); a template FnDef that is neither embedded nor in `copies` (embed it
first); a strip that is not a strip; a designation or sequence number the strip uses already.

Online numbering (normaliser #4) gives a new device its counter; a symbol dropped onto a wire splits it
(normaliser #7). Outcome: the representation. Alias `symbol.place`.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `connect` | array of [`ConnectHint`](#connecthint) | no |  | Accepted autoconnect hints. |
| `copies` | array of any JSON value | no |  | The library documents to embed with the placement (`lib/` JSON form; FT-656): the symbol, the part and their closure as the caller resolved it; empty when the project holds them. |
| `orient` | [`CmdOrient2`](#cmdorient2) | no | `"r0"` | The orientation. |
| `page` | [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) | yes |  | The page. |
| `pos` | [`CmdPt2`](#cmdpt2) | yes |  | The insertion point. |
| `rep_type` | [`RepType`](#reptype) or `null` | no |  | The representation type; default the symbol's. |
| `symbol` | [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) | yes |  | The symbol copy. |
| `target` | [`PlaceTarget`](#placetarget) | yes |  | Which device the representation belongs to. |
| `variant` | integer (format `uint8`, min 0, max 255) | no | `0` | The stored contact-image or CP variant. |

## Types

### CmdOrient2

Orientation: rotation clockwise on the sheet, optionally mirrored (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: one of `"r0"`, `"r90"`, `"r180"`, `"r270"`, `"m0"`, `"m90"`, `"m180"`, `"m270"`

### CmdPt2

A point or a displacement [x, y] in nanometres, y downwards (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: array of (integer (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991), integer (min -9007199254740991, max 9007199254740991)) (at least 2 item(s), at most 2 item(s))

### CmdUuid

A lower-case hyphenated UUID naming a record (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (at least 36 character(s), at most 36 character(s))

Pattern: `^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$`

### ConnectHint

An accepted autoconnect hint, as an explicit connection (ADR-0007: autoconnect is an editing aid; the
command carries the result).

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cp` | integer (format `uint16`, min 0, max 65535) | yes |  | The symbol CP of the new representation (`SymbolCp.idx`). |
| `to` | [`EndpointParam`](#endpointparam) | yes |  | The other end: a CP or a junction. |

### EndpointParam

An endpoint named in command parameters: a function CP, a junction, or a point on an existing
connection (which splits it and creates a junction there, doc 06 §3.5).

JSON: `{"cp": {"function": "…", "idx": 1}}`, `{"junction": {"junction": "…"}}`,
`{"on_connection": {"connection": "…", "at": [x, y]}}`.

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: Connection point `idx` of a function.

   Shape: object { `cp`: object { `function`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `idx`: integer (format `uint16`, min 0, max 65535) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `cp` | object { `function`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `idx`: integer (format `uint16`, min 0, max 65535) } | yes |  |  |

2. **Form 2**: A junction.

   Shape: object { `junction`: object { `junction`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `junction` | object { `junction`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } | yes |  |  |

3. **Form 3**: A point on an existing connection's route.

   Shape: object { `on_connection`: object { `at`: [`CmdPt2`](#cmdpt2), `connection`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `on_connection` | object { `at`: [`CmdPt2`](#cmdpt2), `connection`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } | yes |  |  |

### PlaceTarget

Which device a placed representation belongs to (doc 06 §3.3).

One of the following forms:

1. **Form 1**: A new device with a new main function; its counter comes from online numbering.

   Shape: object { `new_device`: object { `fndef?`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) or `null`, `kind?`: [`DeviceKind`](#devicekind) or `null`, `letter`: [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `new_device` | object { `fndef?`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) or `null`, `kind?`: [`DeviceKind`](#devicekind) or `null`, `letter`: [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident) } | yes |  |  |

2. **Form 2**: Another representation of an existing function (FR-DEV-003).

   Shape: object { `existing_function`: object { `function`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `existing_function` | object { `function`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } | yes |  |  |

3. **Form 3**: A new function of an existing device (FR-DEV-038).

   Shape: object { `join_device`: object { `device`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `fndef?`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) or `null`, `role?`: [`FnRole`](#fnrole) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `join_device` | object { `device`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `fndef?`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) or `null`, `role?`: [`FnRole`](#fnrole) } | yes |  |  |

4. **Form 4**: A new device made from a part copy (part-first placement; FR-UI-017, FR-DEV-017, WP-S2.04 D9): the device `{tag: {letter, counter: none}, parts: [the part, quantity 1]}` and one function per entry of the part's `function_template`; the representation draws entry `template`, the others stay unplaced.

   Shape: object { `from_part`: object { `letter`: [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident), `part`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `template`: integer (format `uint16`, min 0, max 65535) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `from_part` | object { `letter`: [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident), `part`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid), `template`: integer (format `uint16`, min 0, max 65535) } | yes |  |  |

5. **Form 5**: One new terminal of an existing strip, created as `terminal.add` creates it and placed (`device.place` only; AC-28, WP-S2.04 D9).

   Shape: object { `new_terminal`: object { `designation`: [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident), `part?`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) or `null`, `seq?`: integer (format `uint32`, min 0) or `null`, `strip`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } }

   | Name | Type | Required | Default | Description |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | `new_terminal` | object { `designation`: [`CmdIdent`](#cmdident), `part?`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) or `null`, `seq?`: integer (format `uint32`, min 0) or `null`, `strip`: [`CmdUuid`](#cmduuid) } | yes |  |  |

### CmdIdent

An identifier: non-empty, one line, NFC, without leading or trailing white space (doc 05 §3.2).

Type: string (at least 1 character(s))

Pattern: `^[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000](?:[^\u0000-\u001F\u007F-\u009F]*[^\u0000-\u0020\u007F-\u00A0\u1680\u2000-\u200A\u2028\u2029\u202F\u205F\u3000])?$`

### DeviceKind

A device's UI and numbering hint. Doc 03 enumerates only these kinds so far; others are kept as
`DeviceKind::Unknown` until the list is decided.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"psu"` | Power supply. |
| `"terminal"` | Terminal. |
| `"blanking_plate"` | Blank manifold or valve-terminal position (doc 11 §2.7). |

### FnRole

Main or auxiliary function.

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"main"` | The main function (the default). |
| `"aux"` | An auxiliary function. |

### RepType

Representation types (doc 03 §6, doc 07 §2.3). `panel_front` is a symbol type only: panel-front
representations are derived, never stored (ADR-0006 amendment 3).

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `"multi_line"` | Multi-line (the default). |
| `"single_line"` | Single-line. |
| `"overview"` | Overview. |
| `"fluid"` | Fluid. |
| `"topology"` | Bus topology. |
| `"contact_image"` | Contact image. |
| `"panel_front"` | Panel front (symbol graphics only). |
| `"strip_segment"` | Strip segment. |
| `"graphic"` | Graphic. |

## Exit codes

A command runs as one line of a command log replayed by `ew apply` ([doc 17 §3.5](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#35-command-logs-ewcmd)). The exit code of `ew apply` is:

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The line committed as one transaction. |
| 1 | A prevent rule or the command's own domain rule refused the line (`Prevented`, `Rejected`); without `--one-step` the lines before it stay committed and are saved, with `--one-step` nothing is saved. |
| 2 | Anything else stops the replay: invalid parameters, a missing record, an unresolvable reference, an open, lock or save error. |

The codes of every subcommand are in [doc 17 §3.2](https://github.com/Ironkode787/ElektraWatt/blob/main/docs/design/17-extensibility.md#32-exit-codes).
